title: GPU OOM proxy + libmix playlog
content:
Purpose: iterative scratchpad tracking attempts to repro and mitigate an intermittent GPU OOM seen on a subset of machines. Focus is on library mixing (libcuda/libnvidia) + proxy shim interactions and transient NVML timeouts. Not a final writeup — just a step-by-step playlog and hypotheses for follow-ups.

Summary of behavior observed:
- Workload: medium-length chat generation (seq_len 2048 warm cache) under continuous batching.
- Symptom: occasional sudden allocation failure from CUDA at high token steps; process aborts with runtime error and the container is marked unhealthy.
- Not everyone reproduces; appears correlated with mixed driver/lib combinations after recent image rollouts.

Chronological playlog (commands, outputs, notes):

2026-03-11 09:14 - baseline quick-check on host
> uname -a
Linux rdw-node-12 5.19.0-90-generic x86_64 GNU/Linux
> nvidia-smi -q | head -n 20
GPU 0: A100-SXM4 (UUID: GPU-abc123)
Driver Version: 535.86
+ memory usage: 0 MiB (fresh boot)

2026-03-11 09:30 - container run (repro attempt)
docker run --gpus all --rm -it --entrypoint=/bin/bash redwood/serve:canary
# inside container
python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.version.cuda)"
True
"12.1"

Repro run command used repeatedly:
python -m serve.client --model small-chat --batch-size 16 --max-tokens 2048 --profile-all

Observed error (capture):
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.52 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 36.01 GiB already allocated; 1024.00 MiB free; 3.00 GiB cached)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "serve/core/infer.py", line 398, in _dispatch
    out = model.forward(inputs)
  File ".../lib/libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"

Notes: that last "libcuda.so.1" snippet appears mid-stack in some runs — suggests rpath/ldpath weirdness where loader tries to open a specific lib during the stack unwinding.

2026-03-11 10:05 - ldd and library checks
# on host (not container)
ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep -E "libcuda|libnvidia" || true
	libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f...)
	libnvidia-ml.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so.1 (0x00007f...)

# inside container ldd shows different mapping (libcuda missing, shim present)
ldd torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep libcuda || true	
	libcuda.so.1 => not found

Hypothesis: some images still rely on a host-mounted libcuda via volume or driver-proxy (nvidia-container-runtime); if container runtime/entrypoint adjusts LD_LIBRARY_PATH, the process may end up intermittently resolving to host lib vs bundled lib, causing incompatible symbols and OOM behavior.

2026-03-11 10:30 - test with LD_PRELOAD shim to force host lib
# reproduce with explicit preload to see difference
LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 
python -u -m serve.client --model small-chat --batch-size 16 --max-tokens 2048

Result: slightly more consistent runs, fewer OOMs but still one crash after ~20 minutes. Stack now shows:
/opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so(+0x1a2ef) -> symbol lookup error: undefined symbol: _ZN3c105Error...

Interpretation: Preloading host lib resolves "not found" but exposes symbol ABI mismatch in torch -> suggests torch was built against different CUDA/driver headers than host lib provides.

2026-03-11 11:00 - nvml probe and timeouts
# quick probe script to stress NVML calls and watch for timeouts
python -c "import pynvml, time; pynvml.nvmlInit(); h=pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(0);
for i in range(100):
  try:
    print(i, pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo(h).used)
  except Exception as e:
    print('NVML ERR', i, e); break
  time.sleep(0.2)"

Output observed occasionally: NVML ERR 14 pynvml.nvml.NVMLError_LibraryNotFound: NVML Shared Library not found

Note: this only happens inside container when an LD_LIBRARY_PATH overlay is present. Suggests dynamic loader path race or mount/unmount timing during node upgrades.

2026-03-11 13:10 - reproducing with interposer (LD_AUDIT / LD_PRELOAD approach)
# built tiny interposer that logs dlopen/dlsym calls to /tmp/lib-hooks.log
LD_AUDIT=/opt/debug/libaudit.so python -m serve.client ...

Logged sequence: dlopen("/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1") -> dlopen("/opt/driver-shim/libnvidia-compat.so") -> dlsym("cublasCreate_v2") -> failure in compat shim -> fallback -> direct host lib call.

Hypothesis: driver-shim injected by our init (entrypoint tweak) intercepts some symbols and fails to forward properly for cublas/cuBLASLt, leaving partial state that later causes allocation accounting mismatch and OOM.

2026-03-12 09:00 - quick mitigation experiments done in-cluster
- Swapped to image variant that bundles CUDA runtime (not relying on host lib) -> more stable, no OOM in 12h run (but higher startup memory because of duplicate runtime).
- Injected explicit LD_LIBRARY_PATH in startup script to point to /usr/local/cuda/lib64 first -> mixed results; if host driver updated earlier than container, ABI mismatch occurs.

Key hypotheses to validate next:
1) Partial symbol interception by shim leaves NVML/CUDA bookkeeping inconsistent across process boundary, leading to stale cached memory accounting and allocation failures.
2) There is a timing/race where driver library mount becomes briefly invisible to container loader (kicked by kubelet driver mount refresh), causing some processes to start with missing libs, then later components load new libs and mismatch occurs.
3) Our tensor allocator (custom pooling) may be caching pointers from previous driver instance; when driver libs swap underneath, allocator's bookkeeping becomes incorrect and throws OOM on valid memory.

Things I tried (short checklist):
- ldd inside/outside container: confirmed "not found" in container for libcuda sometimes.
- LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/.../libcuda.so.1 to force host lib (reduced frequency).
- LD_AUDIT interposer to capture dlopen/dlsym order (revealed shim activity).
- Swapped to full-bundled-runtime image (stable for 12h).
- Rebuilt small C-extension with same CUDA major/minor to test symbol ABI compatibility (didn't fully reproduce).
- Increased tcmalloc page limits to rule out host OOM -> no change.

Minimal repro notes (next steps to make reliable repro):
- Need machine that previously had driver 535.86 then updated to 536.x and a mix of nodes with older images.
- Create job that starts container during a driver bind-mount refresh (kubelet drain/uncordon simulation) to attempt race reproduction.
- Run interposer + nvml probe in parallel while running memory-heavy workload to catch exact moment of library resolution change.

Immediate mitigations for production:
- Prefer image variants that bundle CUDA runtime into the image for Dedicated nodes where isolation matters.
- Add startup check that ensures all required libs are resolvable before starting process (exit/crash early rather than start partially broken).
- Add sentinel in our init that refuses to run if LD_LIBRARY_PATH points to host libraries unless explicit opt-in flag set.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Diego: can you share the driver upgrade timeline for rdw-node-12 and list nodes that had the overlay mount at 2026-03-09..12? (assigned PROJ-OO-789)
- Ruth: can you run the interposer on one of the failing hosts and push the /tmp/lib-hooks.log to the ticket?
- I will try to craft a small c-repro that uses dlopen/dlsym to simulate partial symbol interception and allocator misuse.

Slack refs: <#infra-oom> thread starting 2026-03-09 (search "libmix"), PR suggested: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4521

Notes-to-self: keep this playlog chronological; once we have a reliable repro, consolidate into a formal postmortem. For now, record commands, outputs, and noisy errors here.

-- Aisha
